Vivek / Redwood team,

We had a significant production incident this morning between 10:10–10:40 UTC where our platform saw a large spike of 5xx and 429 responses from your API. The symptom was amplified by our client-side retries which turned a partial degradation into a retry storm and doubled the effective load. Users experienced timeouts and failed requests across multiple endpoints.

Please treat as high priority.

Alex / team — quick technical summary from triage:
- Timeline: 10:08:22 UTC — 10:39:50 UTC saw elevated 5xx/429 across the primary model shard serving Catalyst traffic.
- Cause: an autoscaler race led to premature KV-cache eviction and a set of cold-starts for multiple inference workers. The sudden cold-paths increased token latencies and triggered throttling on a dependent rate-limiter which returned 429s.
- Amplification: Catalyst client retry policy (short fixed backoff) retried aggressively, creating additional bursts that pushed workers into CPU/queue saturation.
- Quantified impact: we attribute ~42k failed requests during the window; estimated affected token volume ~1.2M; estimated customer-visible errors ~27% of requests for affected endpoints.

Remediation completed at 10:53 UTC: hotfix to autoscaler policy and KV cache warmup backfill deployed. We're also pushing a change to guard against fast client retry amplification (server-side 429 smoothing window).

I'm attaching a preliminary credit calc (proposed_credit_calc.xlsx) with line items: lost requests, excess compute cost, and operational overhead for your team. This is preliminary — Vivek will follow up with the commercial proposal.

— Monica
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
